title: Quadratic Equation
notes: **Quadratic Equation:** This topic covers the fundamental concepts of quadratic equation in the mathematics curriculum.
Understanding quadratic equation is essential for solving problems and building higher-level mathematical skills.
Key definitions and theorems related to quadratic equation should be memorized and practiced regularly.
confusion: The discriminant D=b²-4ac determines the NATURE of roots, not their values. Use the quadratic formula for values.
If D<0, roots are COMPLEX (not "no roots"). They come in conjugate pairs: a+bi and a-bi.
"One root common" is different from "both roots common." Check carefully which case applies.
practice: Find the nature of roots of 2x²-3x+5=0. Also find the roots.
If α,β are roots of x²-5x+6=0, form a quadratic equation whose roots are α² and β².
Find k if the equations x²-kx+12=0 and x²-kx+Kx-12=0 have a common root.
universalFacts: The quadratic formula was known to Babylonian mathematicians over 4000 years ago.
The discriminant concept connects algebra to geometry: D>0 means the parabola crosses the x-axis twice, D=0 means it touches once, D<0 means it never touches.
Quadratic equations model projectile motion, area optimization, and many real-world situations.
